channel.title: The San Francisco Standard - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The San Francisco Standard (sfstandard.com)

item.title: Mayor Lurie meets Eileen Gu. Plus: Concerns after Tenderloin bodyguard fight
item.description: Also in today’s Power Play: a surprising SFPD demotion.

item.title: The Wishlist: Buying a home on an educator’s salary required an act of God
item.description: It took a crash course in home ownership (and a few answered prayers) to find a Bay Area home for $400,000.

item.title: Who’s who in California’s billionaire tax brawl
item.description: A proposed 5% wealth tax on California billionaires has unleashed a wave of anti-tax groups fueled by tech elites.

item.title: SF voted to close juvenile hall. Seven years later, it costs $543K per kid
item.description: Juvenile hall “was never full from the day they cut the ribbon.” But it has turned out to be much more difficult to change course than the city expected.

item.title: At Giants spring training, success isn’t measured in wins
item.description: San Francisco is 13-2 under Tony Vitello, but the manager acknowledges that there’s much more important developments taking place in Scottsdale.

item.title: Wait, Cyprus? What to know about the Transamerica Pyramid’s new owner
item.description: Buy San Francisco skyscraper, they did. Here’s what to know about Yoda PLC, the island company that came out of nowhere.

item.title: Why the 49ers are betting on future Hall of Famer Mike Evans to improve their offense
item.description: Brock Purdy will have a new top target as the veteran wide receiver is expected to sign a three-year contract worth up to $60.4 million.

item.title: ‘No words spoken’: Chinatown stabbing suspect has criminal record, prominent father
item.description: Court records detail a sudden, unprovoked attack in Chinatown as new information emerges about the suspect and his family ties.

item.title: Kawakami: A solid offseason start, but … could the 49ers blow it with Trent Williams?
item.description: Deals with Mike Evans and Vederian Lowe highlighted a reasonable and rationale day for a franchise that’s set up to pursue a few more key additions.

item.title: Police report: Daniel Lurie initiated confrontation that injured his security team
item.description: The mayor jumped out of his car and confronted several men on the street. ‘On whose behalf do I need to move?’ one replied.
